problem: VLAs struggle with complex instructions and new scenes without task-specific fine-tuning, while scene representations offer strong semantics and spatial reasoning but no direct solution for motion and are limited to navigation and pick-and-place.
motivation: Many language queries reduce to a repeated three-step process of object grounding, spatial reasoning, and part-level interaction. Implementing each as a scene query tool lets an LLM agent solve them zero-shot with open-vocabulary generality, and provides a data point in the modular vs end-to-end debate.
key_idea: Expose an open-vocabulary object map with VLM-detected 3D affordances as a small set of tools (object retrieval, spatial queries, affordance-based interact/go_to) that an LLM agent calls with feedback to execute tabletop and mobile manipulation queries zero-shot.
insight: Affordance detection matters once tasks go beyond pick-and-place: the No-Aff ablation (whole-object point cloud) is worse on keyboard, power adapter, thumbtack and drawer queries, and in mobile settings affordance-aware navigation is critical when the object has a preferred approach side. The modular design also allows failure attribution, showing perception (31 queries) as the main bottleneck, while VLAs (~20% success) fail on simpler picks and on spatial language (left/right, near/far, small/large).
method: Object Map: ConceptGraphs-style open-vocabulary map built from MobileSAM masks, CLIP features and back-projected depth point clouds, with objects merged by geometry and semantic similarity; each Object stores point cloud, RGB/depth crops, features and affordances
LLM Agent: LangChain agent with a Gemini backend that sees only a symbolic State (held_object, inventory of string ObjectKeys), not sensor data or the map
Tools: object_retrieval (CLIP top-k=3 then Gemini 2.5 verification), spatial tools (distance_to, distance_between, left_of, right_of, size_of on point clouds), and interact(obj, action)
Affordance detection: Gemini 2.5 predicts (skill, part) pairs from top-k crops, then a bounding box; SAM 2.1 gives a mask which is lifted to 3D with depth; multi-view IoU merging

Skills: motion-planned (MoveIt 2) grasp, place, drop, grasp_part, tip_push, pinch_pull, hook_pull using AnyGrasp and point-cloud normals; ToolOutput with success and feedback_msg enables up to 3 retries, and remapping after failures

Mobile ASP: multi-keyframe map from teleoperated posed RGB-D, go_to tool choosing a free-space pose via footprint cost plus affordance-normal penalty, and local redetection after arrival to handle mapping errors

setting.backbone: Gemini (frozen LLM agent via LangChain); Gemini 2.5 VLM for retrieval verification and affordance detection; CLIP, MobileSAM, SAM 2.1, AnyGrasp
setting.observation: Wrist RGB-D (RealSense D435i) with posed keyframes and odometry (T265) for mobile
setting.action_space: High-level tool calls and skills executed via motion planning (RRT-Connect), Nav2 navigation goals
setting.privileged: none (mobile setting uses a few teleoperated keyframes collected before the policy runs)

numbers_note: Results are only in figures (tabletop success rates over 15 queries x 10 trials, progress rates, mobile results); no numeric tables and no standard navigation benchmarks. Text-only values: pi0-FAST and pi0.5 overall success ~20%; progress in 67% and 75% of cases respectively.
results: ASP outperforms pi0-FAST and pi0.5 (DROID-finetuned) on 13 of 15 real tabletop queries, while the VLAs reach roughly 20% overall success. The affordance ablation hurts on keyboard, power adapter, thumbtack and drawer queries. Mobile ASP handles affordance-aware navigation, double-pick and spatial queries in a room.
limitations: Designed for short-horizon tasks; cannot do long-horizon or complex-motion tasks (fold shirt, clean counter) and skills cover only prismatic drawers
Perception is the main failure source (undersegmentation, wrong affordance detection, unnatural handle grasps); mobile version has no exploration or dynamic remapping and needs teleoperated keyframes
Small-scale real-robot evaluation (10 trials per query), with no standardized benchmark numbers
